If the economy is doing well, will the tax cuts cause inflation?

Possibly but not directly and not to a significant degree.

Some freshman level monetary policy. Inflation is caused by either an increase in the monetary supply (the total amount of money available to the economy) or by an increase in the velocity of money (how many times a dollar changes hand in a given period of time). These both lead to nominal inflation (the price of everything goes up with a concurrent increase in the effective monetary supply). Real inflation or deflation is caused primarily by changes in cost structure likely due to diminished resources relative to demand (think the price of oil over the last 100 years) and generally only effects specific goods or services. So in order for tax cuts to cause inflation they must either increase the monetary supply (which won't happen directly) or increase the velocity of money which could happen but not to any great degree. The real concern with tax cuts and inflation is budget deficits. If the government cuts taxes but needs to borrow/print money to make up the deficit inflation will occur but this is more fundamentally a fiscal policy issue and not a monetary policy issue.
